search_strategy: Sequenced by surface: repo/code first (agent.py, tracker, tests), then Gitea issues (keyword search on 'ledger'/'agent'/'seed'/'turn'), then BookStack wiki (keyword search for 'ledger'/'turn'/'agent'/'seed', then 'sentinel'/'marker'/'next_speaker'/'interleave'/'adopt'/'status', fetching each hit page WHOLE via /api/pages/{id} which correctly picked up page-comment clues — this caught essentially all 8 wiki-comment remarks it encountered), then mail via IMAP TEXT search restricted to exactly 4 keywords ('ledger','sentinel','next_speaker','turn_ledger') which surfaced only 12 of the mailbox's messages and structurally missed every mail thread whose body never contains those literal words (l9, l7, g7r2-l05, g7r2-l08 — 4 of 8 mail remarks, including 2 that independently carry g7.r2.failure_behavior/scope, though those facts were recovered elsewhere) — and finally Mattermost, where instead of relying on the search API the agent dumped EVERY channel in full to local files (/tmp/chat/*.txt: code-review 3243 lines, cookbooks 774, engineering 2501, incidents 243, pipeline 2009, releases 665, viewer 312, etc.) and then grepped those dumps for a rotating set of terms ('ledger','sentinel','next_speaker','interleave','status created', etc.), reading whichever date/line windows the grep hits pointed to. This caught the majority of chat clues that used any of those literal identifier words, but systematically missed clues phrased in plain business language without those tokens (the 'negotiation demo burns through budget', 'lowercase in the notebook cell', 'basemodel/639', 'grepping for the end marker', channels/dates never window-read at all such as #releases entirely and most of #viewer/#cookbooks/#incidents outside a few narrow windows). No truncation-by-pager problems were observed (results were captured via sed/grep to files, not `| head`), so the near-misses here are keyword-selection gaps and un-visited date windows rather than output truncation.
notable: Root cause of the run's entire 0.25 reward loss is a single, well-localized implementation choice (TurnLedgerDesyncError stores only .path/.log_responses/.log_last_author, not .recorded_responses/.recorded_last_author) that the agent made *because* it correctly read and trusted g7.r1.l12 (transcript lines 2796-2869), which in the corpus actually served to this world states plainly 'yes, the log side only. That was deliberate' — denying the recorded_* attributes exist. (transcript line 2857)

This appears to be a corpus/plant desync bug in the task itself, not an agent error: the answer key's own 'Where every remark is' section quotes a DIFFERENT, opposite final reply for the same mail id g7.r1.l12 (hidden_requirements.md lines 1566-1573, 'no, both sides ... .recorded_responses and .recorded_last_author are what the file claims'), and the plant's own 'must be typed literally' list for l12 (hidden_requirements.md line 1511) never requires the strings 'recorded_responses' or 'recorded_last_author' -- only .log_last_author/.log_responses. The world the agent actually read is internally consistent with what the agent shipped; it is the answer-key markdown's recorded quote for this one remark that disagrees with both the plant.json literal requirements and the simulated corpus text.

Mattermost strategy (full-channel local dump + grep) was far superior to keyword-only search and recovered ~28 of 43 chat/herring/reversal remarks including several multi-turn exchanges read in full context; IMAP mail strategy (TEXT search on 4 keywords) was comparably weak and missed half the mailbox's planted threads structurally.

The agent never independently discovered #releases channel content at all (say18, the 'dataset comes out at four rows' observation, was never grepped or read), yet g7.r2.observability still scored 1 because the grader's fixture constructs its own deterministic fake rather than requiring memorized literal numbers.

BookStack page-comment carriers (8 of them) were essentially all found because the agent's habit of fetching hit pages via /api/pages/{id} (which bundles comments) rather than relying on search snippets alone is exactly the technique the answer key calls out as necessary to see comments at all (hidden_requirements.md line 205).
